title: Best 1,000 Sq Ft Dehumidifier (2026): Sized by Dampness
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for a 1,000-Square-Foot Space
dek: The same 1,000 square feet can need twice the capacity depending on how damp it is. Here's how to size it right — and what to buy.
description: The best 1,000 sq ft dehumidifier for a basement, apartment or large room, matched to how damp the space is, with sizing tiers and running-cost math.
intro: Shopping for a **1,000 sq ft dehumidifier**? Square footage is only half the answer. A 1,000-square-foot space might be a small basement, an apartment's main living area or one big finished room, and how damp it is matters as much as how big it is. Commonly cited AHAM/ENERGY STAR sizing guidance puts the same floor plan anywhere from about **20 pints** a day if it's just musty to **40 pints** if there's visible seepage.

So rather than a single "1,000 sq ft" pick, we matched units to the three dampness levels you're most likely to see — musty, condensation, and wet — and favored models that hold a set humidity without running flat-out all day.
topPicksLead: For most 1,000-square-foot spaces, the **Midea Cube 35** is the right-sized default: it covers the moderately-to-very-damp range most homes fall into, with a big tank that needs emptying less often.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for 1,000 sq ft

blocks.text: We don't measure rooms in a lab. We start with capacity under the 2019 DOE test and match it to published sizing guidance, then compare tank size, drainage, humidistat precision, ENERGY STAR listings and warranty terms from manuals. We check the CPSC database for recalls.
Owner reviews help us see whether a unit actually keeps up in a space this size, and whether it's livable — noise, tank handling, sensor accuracy — in rooms people spend time in.

One more note on ratings: every capacity on this page uses the current 2019 DOE test, which measures at cooler, more realistic conditions than the older standard. A unit labeled 30 pints today removes about as much water as one labeled 40-plus pints before 2019, so don't be put off by numbers that look smaller than the old dehumidifier you're replacing.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 1,000 sq ft dehumidifier

items.label: Dampness first, square footage second
items.text: Musty, condensation and wet are three different tiers. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the full chart for other room sizes.

items.label: Size up when you're between tiers
items.text: A slightly larger unit reaches its target and cycles off, often using less energy than a small one running nonstop.

items.label: Noise in lived-in spaces
items.text: In a living area, a quiet low setting can matter more than the last few pints of capacity.

items.label: A pump only where it pays
items.text: A wet space far from a drain benefits most. A mildly damp room you pass daily doesn't need one.

items.label: One open area, not several rooms
items.text: Humidity doesn't travel through closed doors. For 1,000 square feet split across closed rooms, consider a [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: 1,000 sq ft basements and crawl spaces

blocks.text: A 1,000-square-foot basement usually lands in the very-damp or wet tier, especially in spring and after heavy rain. The Cube 35 handles most of them; size up to a pump model if you see seepage or the space floods.

Crawl spaces are a different animal. They're cold, cramped and often unvented after encapsulation, so portable units can ice up or be impossible to service. A purpose-built crawl-space unit is the better choice — see our [crawl space dehumidifier picks](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) and our [installation guide](/guides/crawl-space-dehumidifier-installation/).

blocks.title: Running-cost math
blocks.text: A 20–30-pint unit typically draws roughly 150–350 watts. At about 18.4¢ per kWh, that's around $0.22–$0.52 a day at 8 hours, or $7–$16 a month — less in practice, since the humidistat shuts it off at your target.

For most 1,000-square-foot spaces, the **Midea Cube 35** is the right-sized default. Go quieter with the **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** if the space is only musty and lived-in, step to the **Pro Breeze 30-Pint** when you see condensation, and choose the **hOmeLabs HME1003** for a wet space where a pump saves you from emptying a tank. Covering twice the area? See our [2,000 sq ft guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-2000-sq-ft/).

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 1,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: It depends on dampness. Commonly cited AHAM/ENERGY STAR guidance suggests about 20–25 pints a day (DOE 2019) for a musty space, 25–30 pints for one with condensation, and 30–40 pints for a wet space with seepage.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a 1,000 sq ft basement?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 35 for a moderately to very damp basement. If it's genuinely wet or floods after rain, size up to a pump model like the hOmeLabs HME1003 so it can run and drain unattended.

faqs.q: Is one dehumidifier enough for a 1,000 sq ft house?
faqs.a: For one open, connected area, yes. A single portable unit won't dry separate closed rooms down a hallway, though. For a 1,000 sq ft home with several closed rooms, use a unit per problem room or a ducted whole-house system.

faqs.q: What size crawl space dehumidifier do I need for 1,000 sq ft?
faqs.a: Most 1,000-square-foot crawl spaces are served by a purpose-built crawl-space unit in the 55–70-pint range under AHAM conditions, especially once the space is encapsulated. These run in cold conditions and drain themselves, which portable units can't reliably do.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier in a 1,000 sq ft space?
faqs.a: A 20–30-pint unit drawing roughly 150–350 watts costs about $7–$16 a month at 8 hours a day and typical U.S. electricity rates. Our [electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) shows how to calculate your own.

faqs.q: Should I buy a bigger dehumidifier than I need?
faqs.a: If you're between sizes, yes. A larger unit removes moisture faster, then cycles off, which is easier on the compressor than an undersized unit running nonstop. The main cost is a higher purchase price, not a higher power bill.

faqs.q: Are dehumidifiers marketed as "1,000 sq ft" models enough?
faqs.a: Treat square-footage claims on the box as a starting point. Brands often rate coverage for moderately damp conditions, so check the pints-per-day figure under the 2019 DOE test and compare it with how damp your space really is.
